chunks: And ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī said: I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام

What do you say about a group of people who were traveling, walking along the seashore, when they came upon a dead man, naked, whom the sea had cast ashore, while they themselves were without clothes and had with them only a waist-wrapper? So how should they perform salat over him while he is naked and they do not have any extra cloth with which to shroud him?

He عليه السلام said: 'A grave is dug for him, and he is placed in his burial niche, and bricks are placed over his private parts,' so that his private parts may be covered with bricks and stones, and salat is performed over him, then he is buried.

key_terms.اللَّبِنُ: bricks used here to cover the ʿawrah
key_terms.سَاحِلِ الْبَحْرِ: the seashore where the body was found
key_terms.لَحْدِهِ: his burial niche within the grave

ai.seo_question: How should salat al-janazah be performed for a naked deceased person when no shroud is available?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for the funeral of a deceased person found naked when no extra cloth is available for shrouding. It instructs that his ʿawrah should first be concealed with bricks or stones in the grave, then salat al-janazah is performed over him, and afterward he is buried.
